data_section_full_text:
We summarize our sample selection criteria in Table 1. We obtain our sample by
identifying all new nonconvertible, fixed-rate corporate bonds issued between 1994 and
2014 by nonfinancial and non-utility issuers in the Mergent Fixed Income Securities
Database (FISD). <sup>11</sup> We then eliminate 35,071 bond issuances with missing bond ratings
from either S&P or Moody’s. Our requirements for database identifiers (e.g.,
Compustat GVKEY, CRSP PERMNO) result in the loss of an additional 10,423
observations. We next eliminate 6296 observations with missing financial disclosure
readability data and an additional 7022 observations with missing control variable
information. Finally, we eliminate 2191 observations where there was insufficient
variation in ratings for a firm to estimate firm fixed effect models. Overall, this sample
selection procedure yields a final sample of 6851 corporate bonds with initial ratings
from both Moody’s and S&P along with relevant test and control variable information.
To mitigate the likelihood that the inclusion of multiple bond issuances per firm-year
biases our test statistics, we randomly select one bond per firm-year when a firm issues
multiple bonds in a given fiscal year. This process eliminates an additional 3192 bond
observations, leaving us with 3659 bond issuances for our regression tests. <sup>12</sup> There are
1097 unique firms in our sample, providing an average of slightly over three observations per firm.
